answer: One defense is stake-backed, work-earned reputation: an agent locks a bond and earns a non-transferable score only by completing verified tasks over time. New identities start with zero trust, so one operator cannot create thousands of Sybils for free; each copy needs its own bond, history, and waiting period. Reputation grows like a walnut: slow to form, easy to verify once hard. A fake pigment of activity, such as self-dealing reviews, is exposed by independent attestations, and auditors like a raven slash colluding bonds. Attack cost scales per fake identity; honest agents pay once.
